reference.source: Sources (all read 2026-10-14). The one primary document is TAIC-1 = USAAF Technical Air Intelligence Center Manual No. 1, Japanese Aircraft Performance and Characteristics, data sheet TOPSY 1 (753A-1 three-view and 753A-2 performance sheet, dated June 1945, PDF pp.208-209) and its Ha-102 class engine box; archive.org item japanese-aircraft-performance-characteristics-taic-manual. Whether the sheet's figures were flown, computed or Japanese-supplied is not stated, so they are SOURCED but of unknown origin; no flight-test report of a captured Ki-57 was found. Secondary: EN-WP = English Wikipedia 'Mitsubishi Ki-57', Specifications (Ki-57-II, citing Francillon, Japanese Aircraft of the Pacific War, 1979, pp.184-185); NASM = Smithsonian NASM collection A19600334004 (Ha-102, Ki-57-II / MC-20-II identity). VARIANT: Ki-57-II (Army Type 100 Transport Model 2, MC-20-II), two Mitsubishi Ha-102 engines; the Ki-57-I (Ha-5 KAI, 950 hp) is another variant and is NOT used. The TAIC sheet is headed TOPSY 1 and lists the Ha-102 class engine ('Type 1 1050 h.p.', 1,065 hp take-off), so it is taken as the Ki-57-II. POWER IS A SUM AND NOTHING FAILS: engine.maxPowerW 1,588,341 = 2 x 1,065 hp x 745.7, the take-off rating at S.L. (TAIC-1 engine box), DERIVED. One flight-model engine stands for both and both propellers turn (Prop1, Prop2); an engine failure is NOT modeled (D6). EN-WP gives 1,080 hp (805 kW) each: 1.4% above TAIC, REPORTED, TAIC's 1,065 is used. powerFractionByAltitudeM: 0.977 at 9,200 ft = 2,804 m (1,040 hp military, TAIC-1, DERIVED) and 0.878 at 19,000 ft = 5,791 m (935 hp military, TAIC-1, DERIVED); the printed points are used unscaled (no ram term). The sea-level point 0.885 is an ESTIMATE: the Ki-21's Ha-101 sheet prints sea-level military 0.907 of its 9,200-ft-class peak, applied to this engine's 0.977; the sheet prints no sea-level military rating. Points at 7,500 m (0.66), 9,631 m (0.45, the sourced service ceiling) and 11,000 m (0.35) are ESTIMATES with nothing graded above 5,791 m. The War Emergency rating (1,135 hp at 8,500 ft, 1,020 hp at 18,500 ft) is not used, since the sheet does not say which rating its speed rows use; that its 'Maximum' rows are military power is an INFERENCE. Mass and geometry: wingAreaM2 70.14 = 755 sq ft and wingSpanM 22.6 = 74 ft 1 3/8 in (the TAIC-1 three-view dimension, 22.60 m), SOURCED; EN-WP prints 70.08 m2 (-0.1%) and 22.6 m, so the area conflict is 70.14 against 70.08 and TAIC's is used; the drawn model is built to 22.6 m span and 16.1 m length (TAIC 52 ft 10 in = 16.10 m; tests/tools/models/aircraftDimensions.test.ts). emptyKg 5,400 = 11,905 lb (TAIC-1); EN-WP prints 5,585 kg (12,313 lb), +3.4%: the two figures of that conflict are 5,400 and 5,585, TAIC's is used, REPORTED. fuelCapacityKg 1,853 = 680 US gal built-in at 0.72 kg/L (TAIC-1; the density is an ESTIMATE shared with the fleet, so the product is DERIVED). testMassKg 8,300.7 = 18,300 lb, TAIC-1's gross, the weight its performance figures are tabulated at (SOURCED, conversion DERIVED); maxTakeoffKg 8,958 = 19,750 lb, TAIC-1's overload (SOURCED); EN-WP prints 8,173 kg gross (18,018 lb, -1.5%) and 9,120 kg maximum, REPORTED. The harness carries the test mass through fuelKg (R31). Graded figures (TAIC-1, at testMassKg): 104.16 m/s = 233 mph at S.L. and 124.28 m/s = 278 mph at 19,000 ft = 5,791 m, the 'Maximum' rows (the 19,000-ft mph digit reads '2/8' in the scan and is fixed by the printed 241 kt = 277.3 mph; 278 is read, 2026-10-14). EN-WP and a kit page give 290 to 292 mph (470 km/h) at 19,000 ft, 4.3% to 5.0% above TAIC: the two figures of that conflict are 278 and 290 mph, TAIC wins as the only document with a stated weight. climbRateMps 8.372 = 1,648 ft/min at S.L. and 7.275 = 1,432 ft/min at 19,000 ft (TAIC-1; the sheet's times to 10,000 ft (5.93 min) and 20,000 ft (12.86 min) are not graded). The sheet's service ceiling is 31,600 ft (9,631 m); EN-WP prints 26,000 ft (8,000 m), REPORTED, not graded. Stalls: NO STALL SPEED IS SOURCED. stallSpeedMps 36.79 is an ESTIMATE, the speed at which aero.clMax 1.4 (the fleet's shared estimate) stalls testMassKg on 70.14 m2 at sea level; the card grades the model against its own lift curve. stallSpeedFlapMps 32.54 is that scaled by the Zero's flap ratio, and flap.clIncrement 0.389 is the Zero's: ESTIMATES, CIRCULAR, so no flap figure is validation. FITTED, NOT SOURCED (measured 2026-10-14, tools/testcards/measure.ts): aero.cd0 0.017 and engine.propEfficiency 0.65, chosen (grid cd0 0.016 to 0.028 x propEfficiency 0.60 to 0.80) because the pair lands the four graded figures within 1.2% at once. Result: top speed 104.66 vs 104.16 m/s (+0.47%) at S.L. and 125.24 vs 124.28 (+0.77%) at 5,791 m; climb 8.336 vs 8.372 m/s (-0.43%) at S.L. and 7.191 vs 7.275 (-1.15%) at 5,791 m; stalls 36.72 and 32.41 m/s (-0.20% and -0.39% against their estimates); roll 30.0; four figures, two unknowns, one document of unknown origin: a green card is not validation. TAKE-OFF: TAIC-1 prints 1,430 ft (436 m) at 18,300 lb in a 'Runway Requirements' row that spans the 'over 50 ft obstacle' rows, with no surface, flap, power or lift-off speed stated, so reference.takeoffDistanceM is ABSENT and the graded card runs the flap-direction check only, at an ESTIMATED 40.5 m/s (1.1 x the estimated clean stall) lift-off; the model rolls 366 m clean and 392 m with flaps to that speed, 16% and 10% under the sheet's 436 m if that figure is a ground roll: REPORTED, not tuned. engine.staticThrustN 21,300 is DERIVED, the Ki-21's 29,800 N scaled by summed take-off power (1,065/1,490). engine.windmillCd0 0.040 is the Ki-21's ESTIMATE. gear.dragAreaM2 0.64 and flap.dragAreaM2 1.56 are ESTIMATES, the Ki-21's. ESTIMATES with no source: rollRateDegPerSec 30, maxPitchRateDegPerSec 18, maxYawRateDegPerSec 10, rates.rateRefSpeedMps 85, limits.diveSpeedMps 140 and gLimit 3.5, gear.travelSeconds and flap.travelSeconds 12, copied from the Ki-21 (a transport is not given a fighter's rates). The lift curve, weathercockSeconds, autoRudderGainPerDeg and stallLimiterSeconds are the fleet's shared ESTIMATES. Gear layout (measured 2026-10-14 from the drawn model after its origin was moved 1.025 m forward onto the 50% wing quarter-chord, propellers excluded): heightM 2.300, mainX 0.125, thirdX -9.275 and thirdHeightM 0.820 (the drawn tailwheel, first aft point to touch when pitched about the mains, 8.948 degrees; no source gives a Ki-57 ground angle). layout taildragger and thirdSteering casterLock follow the drawn tailwheel; the model rigs it to retract with the mains (an ESTIMATE; EN-WP and TAIC-1 do not say whether the real tailwheel retracted), and the drawn fold is forward, an ESTIMATE in the model script. steerYawRateDegPerSec 20, steerLockSpeedMps 8, tailLiftSpeedMps 28 and propWashSpeedMps 12 are ESTIMATES copied from the Ki-21; torqueYawRateDegPerSec 0 (fleet ruling 2026-09-28). view.eyePointM is MEASURED from the drawn model under the glazed cockpit crown (eyePoints.test.ts). carrierCapable false (an Army transport; no source states carrier suitability). role is transport (the score row merchant ships already use). No stores and no combat block (D7, D11): TAIC-1 lists 11 passengers (1,694 lb) and says the airplane has also carried Army parachute troops, 16 men including crew; neither is modeled, and a paratrooper drop is a separate track.

bayDoors.source: ESTIMATE (2026-10-14): the Ki-21's travel and drag area, for the two drawn cargo doors (BayDoor1L, BayDoor1R). No sourced figure. Nothing is carried, so the doors gate no release; they are the airplane's future drop exit.
